title: I have an idea for a cosmic RPG — would you actually play something like this?
author: GeSS997
selftext:
I've been thinking about this game concept for quite a while, and I'd really like to know if the idea sounds interesting to anyone besides me. I'm not looking for developers or funding right now. I just want some honest feedback before I take the concept any further.

Right now I just want to answer one question:

**Does the concept itself sound fun?**

The game would be a **third-person RPG-shooter set in a cosmic-fantasy universe**, combining planetary exploration, companions, story choices and a character progression system based on weapon combinations rather than traditional classes.

# The setting

Magic and advanced technology coexist across a galaxy connected by an ancient network of portals.

The portals were created by a mysterious civilization known as the **Architects**.

They disappeared long ago, leaving behind impossible technologies, ruins and artifacts that modern civilizations barely understand.

The player starts as an ordinary person caught in a conflict between several factions.

While trying to escape slavery, they discover an ancient artifact known as the **Architect Core**.

That discovery changes everything.

# No traditional classes

Instead of choosing Warrior / Mage / Rogue, your character gradually develops based on how you actually play.

You can equip **two weapons at the same time**.

For example:

* Rifle + energy shield
* Sword + rune gauntlet
* Staff + revolver
* Bow + magic weapon

The important part isn't simply having two weapons. It's **how they interact with each other**. Different combinations create different combat styles. One combination might focus on mobility, another on crowd control, another on burst damage, another on defense and counterattacks.

The more you actually use a weapon combination, the more its **synergy develops**, unlocking new possibilities. The goal isn't to grind individual weapons, but to let the game naturally reward the playstyles you enjoy using.

# The Architect Core

The Core is the main progression system.

It gradually unlocks:

* active abilities
* passive Protocols
* weapon synergies
* stat upgrades
* weapon modifications
* exploration abilities
* new interactions with the environment

The idea is that you don't permanently lock yourself into one build.

You can collect different abilities and Protocols and change your active setup depending on what you're doing. One setup for exploration. Another for normal combat. Another for a difficult boss.

So instead of progression being:

>Level 20 → +10% damage

I'd like it to feel more like:

>"What kind of playstyle do I want to build?"

# Exploration

The game wouldn't be one enormous empty open world. Instead, planets would contain relatively compact open areas filled with things worth discovering:

* ancient ruins
* dungeons
* hidden locations
* settlements
* merchants
* side quests
* secrets
* unique technologies
* optional encounters

Exploration should actually reward curiosity.

# Companions & story

You would travel with companions who have their own abilities, personalities, stories and relationships with the protagonist. They wouldn't just be walking damage dealers — they'd also have their own opinions and could influence certain story outcomes.

The main story would eventually expand far beyond the initial conflict, involving the Architects, the origin of the Core and events that happened to the galaxy long before the game begins.

But the lore isn't really what I'm asking about.

What I want to know is:

* Would you actually play this?
* Which part sounds the most interesting?
* Does the weapon-combination system sound like something you'd enjoy building a character around?
* Does anything here sound unnecessarily complicated or generic?
* If you wouldn't play it, **what is the biggest reason why?**

And please be honest.

If your reaction is **"this sounds like another generic RPG"**, I'd genuinely like to know what gives you that impression.

**I want to find out whether there's actually a game here that people would want to play.**

Thanks for reading, and I'd really appreciate any feedback!😊

**GenAI Disclosure:**  
I used generative AI to help refine the wording of this post and create illustrative concept art. The game concept, gameplay mechanics, setting and overall design are my own. The game itself does not rely on or require GenAI.

comments.author: Viktorkin
comments.body: I don't think any of this matters in the slightest until someone sees the game. Great premise does not equal good game. I spent 4 hours the other day playing a game where you clean up a library. Game just needs to be good.

replies.author: CaptainKatapult
replies.body: sounds awesome, what's the name of the clean up game?

comments.author: Legal_Suggestion4873
comments.body: Since you're using AI to do all this, you should just ask claude to pretend to be a bunch of different people and feed this prompt into it. Complete the cycle!

replies.author: Accomplished-Sea3176
replies.body: On that note, I remember trying to see if I could get AI to act as a playtester for a puzzle game prototype I was working on. I had it dispatch subagents that could interact with the game via a simple API, and they could 'see' the game via text descriptions of the scenes and interactables. I had rounds of subagents play through the game and had an orchestrator tune the puzzle difficulty to be challenging but not impossible. After a few hours I tried the fully tuned puzzle to see how it worked out. I was able to solve it in about 30 seconds by just clicking every interactable button until it solved. And of course the main orchestrator was like "Of course, you're so right to point that out, that was a seam the agents didn't discover, and that's on me". So I guess we're a long ways away before LLMs can give good feedback lol

comments.author: NovaGuarda
comments.body: You're like 0.05% done with this. You'll understand when you start making it.
